report.title: 4th EEAS Report on Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference Threats
report.licence: EEAS legal notice: reuse is authorised provided the source is acknowledged (third-party material excepted)
report.pages_note: Pages are the report's printed page numbers. The PDF has 40 pages and puts the network graph on one spread, so printed 28 is PDF page 25, 29 is 26, 30-31 is 27, 33 is 29 and 34 is 30; printed 14 is PDF page 12.

entered_by: Claude (Undertow build session), read from the PDF text (pdftotext 14 Nov 2026)
checked_by: A second machine reading, not a person's check: Claude (Undertow session) on 15 Nov 2026 read every row against printed pp. 28-34 and p. 14 of the PDF (sha256 matched). Four quotes were put back to the report's exact words, the RRN region corrected, five targets from pp. 32 and 34 added and two origin bases reworded, each after analyst review.
rule: One row per Information Manipulation Set (IMS) the report names and describes in 'Infrastructures and Information Manipulation Sets (IMS) in 2025' (pp. 28-31) and 'Cheap and fast: the use of AI in Chinese FIMI operations' (p. 34). Targets the report names for those IMS on p. 32 ('Ukraine: a persistent target of Russian FIMI') are added with the page. Quotes are the report's words, short, with the page. 'Aligned' is recorded as alignment, never as origin: the report itself calls Storm-1516 and Operation Overload non-attributed. Origin is set only where the report names who operates the IMS. Domains, outlet names and the names of individuals in the report are left out.

operations.name: Doppelgänger
operations.attribution_wording: operated by the EU-sanctioned entities Social Design Agency (SDA) and Struktura
operations.origin_basis: operators named (Social Design Agency and Struktura, 'EU-sanctioned entities', p. 28); the report places Doppelgänger among the layers of the Russian FIMI ecosystem (p. 32)
operations.target_text: expanded its target audience to include Hebrew-speaking communities (p. 28); Ukrainian audiences targeted through newly created domains impersonating Ukrainian media outlets (p. 32)

behaviours.text: focuses on impersonating legitimate media outlets
deployed fewer typo-squatted domains
seeks to build legitimacy by impersonating established outlets

operations.name: RRN/Media Brands
operations.target_text: around five websites targeting Germany, France, Italy, Poland, Turkey, the United States (US), and the Middle East and North Africa

behaviours.text: centred on the creation of inauthentic media brands
published an estimated average of 15 articles per week, many AI-generated

operations.name: Operation Overload
operations.attribution_wording: Also known as Matryoshka, this non-attributed but Russia-aligned IMS
operations.target_text: expanded to Poland and Romania ahead of their elections; Armenia and Moldova received nearly half of the impersonation videos; France, Germany and Ukraine remained targets

behaviours.text: posting fake content like impersonation videos and deceptively redirecting to inauthentic articles
The usual amplification pattern on X and Bluesky relies on two sets of coordinated inauthentic accounts
While Overload continues to rely primarily on CIB channels on X, distribution via Telegram increased noticeably in 2025.
Storm-1516 and Overload use AI-generated videos easily identifiable as inauthentic

operations.name: Storm-1516
operations.attribution_wording: Also known as CopyCop or False Façade, this nonattributed Russia-aligned IMS
operations.target_text: networks dedicated to German, American, French, Moldovan or general audiences; Moldovan, Ukrainian, German and Armenian leaderships (p. 29); messages during the Polish Presidential elections (p. 32)

behaviours.text: uses fabricated websites, legitimate media platforms, online influencers and various amplification accounts
fictional news outlets, then websites spoofing authentic media or other entities
increasingly relied on a network of contracted influencers
Storm-1516 and Overload use AI-generated videos easily identifiable as inauthentic

operations.name: Portal Kombat
operations.attribution_wording: Also known as Pravda network, it is one of the most prolific Russia-aligned IMS
operations.origin_basis: the report says Russia-aligned and does not name an operator
operations.target_text: sub-domains dedicated to countries and regions, such as the Basque Country, Republika Srpska in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Balkans (p. 29); subdomains targeting African audiences (p. 32)

behaviours.text: pretending to be a media content aggregator
disseminated around 10,000 articles a day across 101 websites

operations.name: Spamouflage
operations.origin_basis: the report says Chinese-aligned and posting state messaging; no operator named
operations.target_text: dissidents and opposition voices; AI-generated cartoons used to target both the EU and the US (p. 34)

behaviours.text: seeder accounts impersonating dissidents, which post a video or an image containing false allegations
newly created, repurposed, or hijacked social media accounts that post and amplify state messaging across more than 50 platforms
the use of AI-assisted impersonation videos
frequently share AI-generated cartoons

operations.name: Paperwall
operations.attribution_wording: launder content originating from the Chinese state through a network of inauthentic news websites leveraged by the public relations firm Haimai
operations.origin_basis: the report says Paperwall launders 'content originating from the Chinese state' (p. 34) and calls it Chinese state-aligned (p. 29); it names the public relations firm Haimai but does not give Haimai's country
operations.target_text: new audiences, mostly in Africa and the Middle East, but also Southeast Asia and Australia

behaviours.text: a network of inauthentic news websites
likely uses automated processes to populate its websites with filler content

operations.name: HaiEnergy
operations.origin_basis: the report says Chinese state-aligned; no operator named for HaiEnergy

behaviours.text: continued their content dissemination activities in 2025

operations.name: Falsos Amigos
operations.attribution_wording: a network of about twelve seemingly independent websites is in fact linked to Chinese state-controlled media
operations.origin_basis: linked to a named state-controlled outlet (CGTN)

behaviours.text: These sites used AI to conceal their ties to the government by disguising the origin of their content and publishing state-sponsored articles as original ones.
Generative tools have been used for the creation of profile pictures, website logos, and favicons
uses AI to paraphrase and translate CGTN content to produce new, seemingly authentic articles
